text:
nora: Quick regroup on the validator surface for model onboarding. Need a compact contract so intake stays fast but we get meaningful async coverage.

ben: Short list: intake does tokenizer probe, shape check, tiny smoke gen (2 tokens), and signature/hash validation. Anything heavier goes to bench-runner. Keep intake <250ms.

rik: Agreed. Proposing the intake response schema: `status: pass|warn|fail`, `async_job: id or null`, `meta: {fingerprint, size_bytes}`. Intake should always return a job id when async checks scheduled.

hana: For async results we must standardize metrics: p50, p95 latency, throughput_tps, peak_mem_mb, golden_jsd, top_n_mismatch. Also include `artifact_paths` list. Bench infra to own bucket paths.

nora: Sampling policy idea: default lightweight async for all, but escalate to full golden/quant when rules hit (new tokenizer, >100M params, first time from submitter). Rules are configurable.

ben: Fallback policy: runtime should auto-fallback to pinned_stable when golden_jsd > threshold OR p95 regress > 1.3x baseline AND mismatch > 0.12. Trigger an alert to oncall and create an incident ticket automatically.

ops-bot: Heads up: bench-runner capacity will be limited 2026-07-12 01:00 UTC for maintenance. Jobs queued then may be delayed ~40m.

rik: Who owns alerts/queries? Suggest eng-ml owns metric schema and alert thresholds, eng-sre owns oncall runbooks and escalation. We'll draft PromQL examples.

hana: I'll draft JSON schema + sample Grafana panel and include example alert rules (p95 delta > 25% over baseline for 30m => page).

nora: Action items: hana -> telemetry schema + panels; rik -> intake response contract RFC; ben -> sampling rule prototype and fallback knobs; nora -> consolidation note + timeline. I'll post a short follow-up with the YAML config tonight.

ben: SGTM.

rik: SGTM.

hana: SGTM.

nora: thanks all, closing thread for now.
